issue.title: Full-history query_agent_artifact_index (~11-12 s at 15.7k rows) keeps bead_claim_checks at ~33 s per run

task_type_fields.impact: `bead_claim_checks` runs of ~33 s overrun the 10 s `waits` routine every tick, delaying bead-claim reconciliation and `epic_launch_flush`. Any other caller of the full-history index query pays ~12 s per call on a long-lived host.
task_type_fields.repro:
Measured read-only on athena on 2026-10-07 while planning sase-1hf (16.8k ace-run artifacts across 37 projects):

- The Rust `query_agent_artifact_index` full-history query takes ~11-12 s for 15.7k ace-run rows with any option set. `agent_scan_wire_from_dict` decode adds ~2.5 s, `asdict` rows ~2 s, and `WaitDependencyIndex.add_many` ~3 s. An active-tier-only query takes 2.3 s.
- Rust `scan_agent_artifacts` with `include_waiting` takes ~12 s.
- The Python filesystem walk of every project's ace-run dirs takes 0.25 s, and reading every agent_meta.json takes ~2-2.5 s.

`bead_claim_checks` still uses the full-history index query: `query_ace_run_index_records` in `src/sase/scripts/_chop_bead_claim_scan.py`, called through `src/sase/scripts/_chop_incremental_index.py`. That likely explains its ~33 s runs. sase-1hf moved `wait_checks` and `sidecar_auto_sync` off the index route. `bead_claim_checks` remains on it, in the 10 s `waits` routine.

Repro: time `query_ace_run_index_records(sase_projects_dir())` in a read-only Python snippet on a host with ~15k ace-run artifacts. Compare it with `sase.axe.wait_marker_scan.scan_waiting_markers(sase_projects_dir())`.

Fix direction (sase-core per the Rust core boundary): make the full-history index query scale (avoid the full decode/scan per call, or serve a narrow pre-launch/claim projection). Otherwise move `bead_claim_checks` to a filesystem or active-tier route as sase-1hf did for `wait_checks`.

Proposed by phase bead sase-1hf.5 (lane-split) in PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1, item 2. Also the unaddressed "check bead_claim_checks's 33 s runtime" item from task sase-1hd. Filed by the sase-1hf land agent.
